chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Alaa, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who carried his wife while he was in the state of Ihram, and he emitted pre-seminal fluid (madh) or seminal fluid (mani). He said: 'If he carried her or touched her with desire, whether he emitted fluid or not, whether he emitted madh or mani, he must shed blood (damm). But if he carried her or touched her without desire, whether he emitted fluid or not, there is no penalty upon him.'

key_terms.دَمٌ: A specific expiation penalty, typically a camel
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man in Ihram who touches his wife with desire?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the juristic distinction between mere physical contact and sexual emission during Hajj. The ruling hinges on the presence of *shahwah* (sexual desire): if intimacy occurs with desire, the pilgrim must offer *damm* (typically a camel), whereas contact without desire incurs no penalty, highlighting the Shia emphasis on intentionality in ritual law.
